result: All 8 output CSVs identical to the 2026-11-02 originals (1,022 numbers, maximum difference 0)

what_was_done: Read the scoring scripts and the weight files
result: One-sample MR within UK Biobank with genome-wide polygenic scores (SBayesRC, millions of SNPs) as single instruments. Not a SNP-level analysis; the step childhood-obesity score -> menarche is a score-outcome association, not an estimate per unit of childhood body size

what_was_done: Traced each score to its GWAS
result: Childhood obesity (Bradfield 2019) and childhood BMI (Vogelezang 2020): no UK Biobank. Menarche score: Guan 2025 direct-effect weights, estimated entirely in UK Biobank (complete overlap; the header of ukbb_mr_puberty_pathway.R says so but the draft text does not). Adult BMI (Yengo 2018) and height (Yengo 2022) covariate scores: include UK Biobank
conclusion_holds: no for the menarche score as used in the draft

what_was_done: Allele score of 92 independent genome-wide significant SNPs from Perry 2014 (ReproGen, no UK Biobank), external weights; same 238,681 women
result: Menarche -> height 0.096 SD per year (0.081 to 0.110) vs 0.094 with the UK Biobank-trained score; direct effect of the childhood-obesity score 0.0138 vs 0.0136; through menarche -0.0117 vs -0.0114

what_was_done: F statistic of every instrument in the MR sample
result: Childhood-obesity score on menarche F = 1,417 (R2 0.6%); on recalled body size at 10 F = 4,413 (R2 1.8%); Perry allele score on menarche F = 6,246 (R2 2.6%); UK Biobank-trained menarche score F = 5,526 (R2 2.3%, inflated by overlap). SNP instruments: mean F 48 (childhood BMI, 16 SNPs), 57 (childhood obesity, 9 SNPs), 53 (menarche, 92 SNPs)

what_was_done: All steps (score -> menarche, menarche -> height, direct, total) refitted in the same 238,681 non-carrier women with age at menarche; the earlier scripts used all women (238,928 incl. carriers) for the menarche first stage
result: Estimates unchanged to the third decimal (menarche -> height Wald 0.0930 in both)

what_was_done: Same models without the height polygenic score as covariate (Perry allele score as menarche instrument)
result: Menarche -> height doubles: 0.198 SD per year (0.181 to 0.214) vs 0.096. Direct effect of the childhood-obesity score 0.032 vs 0.014; through menarche -0.024 vs -0.012; TOTAL becomes +0.008 (0.004 to 0.012; p = 5e-05) instead of +0.002 (p = 0.21)
conclusion_holds: partly: direction of every arrow holds, sizes roughly double, and the statement that the two paths cancel (total = 0) holds only with the height-score adjustment

what_was_done: Same models with the adult-BMI score (Yengo 2018) added
result: Score -> menarche -0.077 years per SD (was -0.122); menarche -> height 0.090; direct +0.021; through menarche -0.007; total +0.014 (p = 1e-14)
conclusion_holds: partly: all arrows hold in direction; total effect is positive, not zero

what_was_done: Childhood-BMI score (Vogelezang 2020) in place of the childhood-obesity score
result: Score -> menarche -0.126 years per SD; direct +0.010 (0.006 to 0.014); through menarche -0.012; total -0.001 (p = 0.38)

check: 10 Two-sample MR: childhood BMI -> age at menarche
what_was_done: 16 SNPs from Vogelezang 2020 (no UK Biobank), SNP-menarche effects estimated in the 238,681 women
result: IVW -0.59 years per SD of childhood BMI (-0.76 to -0.42; p = 2e-11); weighted median -0.66 (p = 9e-29); MR-Egger -0.45 (-1.13 to 0.23; intercept p = 0.68). Bradfield 9 SNPs: IVW -0.26 years per log-odds (p = 1e-07). Strong heterogeneity (Q p = 6e-46)

check: 11 Two-sample MR: age at menarche -> adult height
what_was_done: 92 SNPs from Perry 2014, SNP-height effects estimated in the 238,681 women (no height-score adjustment)
result: IVW 0.18 SD per year later (0.13 to 0.23; p = 3e-12); weighted median 0.21 (p = 9e-39); MR-Egger 0.46 (0.28 to 0.64) with intercept p = 0.002; heterogeneity Q p = 4e-145. Perry effects replicate in UK Biobank (slope 1.05)
conclusion_holds: partly: direction holds with every method; the size is uncertain (0.09 to 0.46 SD per year) and MR-Egger indicates directional pleiotropy

what_was_done: Height regressed on SNP effects on childhood BMI and on menarche together (95 SNPs, IVW)
result: Childhood BMI direct +0.10 SD per SD (0.01 to 0.19; p = 0.028); menarche 0.21 SD per year (0.15 to 0.27). With Bradfield childhood obesity: direct +0.075 per log-odds (p = 3e-04). Univariable total effect of childhood BMI on height: IVW +0.02 (p = 0.64)
conclusion_holds: yes (direct effect positive; total not different from zero)

what_was_done: Scores tested against mother smoking around birth and dark hair colour in the MR sample (height score, age, 10 PCs adjusted)
result: Menarche instruments pass both (Perry score p = 0.98 and 0.16; UK Biobank-trained score p = 0.74 and 1.0). Childhood-obesity score is associated with maternal smoking (+0.0037 per SD, p = 2e-04; hair p = 0.49); childhood-BMI score with both (p = 0.002, 0.004); adult-BMI score strongly with maternal smoking (p = 9e-114)
conclusion_holds: no for the childhood adiposity scores (small but real association with a pre-birth family variable: dynastic or population effects)

check: 14 Positive control: comparative height at age 10
what_was_done: Scores tested against being taller than average at age 10
result: Childhood-obesity score: taller at 10 (+0.027 per SD, p = 9e-91). Later-menarche scores: shorter at 10 (Perry -0.031, p = 4e-117) but taller as adults (+0.021 SD, p = 2e-36), the pattern expected from pubertal timing

check: 15 Pleiotropy of the menarche instruments with childhood body size
what_was_done: Menarche scores tested against recalled body size at 10
result: Perry score -0.034 categories per SD (p = 8e-127); UK Biobank-trained score -0.020 (p = 4e-44): the menarche instruments also lower childhood body size, so menarche -> height is not free of the childhood-adiposity path unless adjusted (2SLS with the exposure score as covariate; multivariable MR, checks 4 and 12)

what_was_done: Height on the Box-Cox within-sex scale (as in the body-size panel) instead of the linear residual
Score -> adult height in 207136 non-carrier men
result: Childhood-obesity score +0.005 SD (p = 0.012); Perry later-menarche score +0.007 SD (p = 2e-04; women +0.021): the puberty-timing score also acts in men, weaker

result: -1.31 years of menarche per category (observational -0.42): three times the observational slope, so the recalled 3-level answer is too coarse a measure of the exposure to scale by; not used in the figure
